hypotheses.primary: On the primary book, the delta-supervised network with simulation fallback (nn_diff hybrid) passes the accuracy gate and takes less wall time than the fastest non-neural route that passes it.
hypotheses.secondary: The same comparison for the network that learns the correction to the lower bound (nn_residual hybrid).
hypotheses.stretch: A hybrid that passes the gate is at least ten times faster than the fastest non-neural route that passes it.

accuracy_gate: Over all contract and scenario pairs, the median across runs of the 99th percentile absolute price error divided by strike is at most tolerance.price_bp basis points, and of the 99th percentile absolute delta error is at most tolerance.delta, both against the book reference.
decision_rule: Comparator is the fastest route with no network, fast_only or hybrid, that passes the gate on the primary book. A hypothesis holds only if its route passes the gate and its mean wall time is below the comparator's by more than the sum of the two standard deviations across runs. Otherwise it is reported as not supported. The bespoke book is a sensitivity run and does not change the verdict.
workload: 42 scenarios: spot shifts -20, -10, -5, 0, 5, 10, 20 percent crossed with vol shifts -30, -15, 0, 15, 30, 50 percent, on a 500 contract book. Primary book uses standard tenors, so vol and maturity pairs repeat. Bespoke book uses whole-day maturities.
comparison_conditions: Same machine, 64-bit floats, the whole job as one batch, six PyTorch threads where PyTorch is used. Hybrid wall time includes building simulation paths.
metrics: median and 99th percentile absolute price error over strike
median and 99th percentile absolute delta error
jobs to recover the upfront cost
unit_of_replication: One run, pairing a network training seed with a simulation seed.
